28: That it is impossible there should not be among them one, etc. — The Sma wrote: and this is not the "gamir and savir," etc., and it is obvious, as is proven explicitly in the Gemara and poskim. However, one can say that we do at least require [one who is] gamir, and so implies the plain language of the Gemara, "one who is gamir," etc., and so wrote the Maharam Paduah in a responsum, siman 43. And the Bach challenged him, that we do not require fully gamir but rather somewhat gamir, and through that he knows some of the reasonings in the dinim, etc. — but his words are not compelling, see there. And see the responsa of Ibn Lev, first volume, siman 123, end of daf 151, where he wrote that the muchzak (one in possession) can claim "kim li" like the Rameh, that we require all three to be gamir. But this does not appear correct to me; rather the words of the Rosh appear primary in the Gemara. And it is possible that even the Rameh concedes, and means specifically that there be among them those who are gamir — for therefore the Tur wrote "and it appears from his words," that is, that it so appears on the surface, but it is not so compelling. And so implies the view of R' Zerachya Halevi and the Ramban and the rest of the poskim that I brought below in siman 25, that it suffices when there is among them one who is gamir — see there, and this is primary.
